images.title: Four triangles, four equal areas
images.purpose: Shows the diagonals of an 8 cm by 6 cm rectangle making four triangles that differ in shape but each have 12 cm².
images.composition: One rectangle, large and centred, with both diagonals crossing at O.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A rectangle 8 units wide and 6 units tall. Both diagonals drawn as dark lines, crossing at the centre point O. Four triangles: the top and bottom triangles (base 8, wide and flat) are filled teal (#0072B2); the left and right triangles (base 6, tall and thin) are filled amber (#E69F00). A small dot at O. Labels: O beside the centre; 8 cm under the bottom side; 6 cm beside the right side; 12 cm² inside each of the four triangles. Check: 8 × 6 = 48 and 48 ÷ 4 = 12; top triangle 1/2 × 8 × 3 = 12, side triangle 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Different shapes, same area: each triangle is 12 cm².
images.description: Shows the diagonals of an 8 cm by 6 cm rectangle making four triangles that differ in shape but each have 12 cm².
images.context: Matches the worked example: 8 cm by 6 cm rectangle, four triangles of 12 cm².
images.teaching_notes: Ask first which triangle looks bigger, then reveal the equal labels.

image_decisions.why: The surprise is visual: non congruent triangles with equal areas inside one rectangle.
